Posterior simulation of stochastic frontier coefficients

Source: R/add_posterior_coefficients.R
add_posterior_coefficients.Rd

Runs the Gibbs sampler on a model prepared by create_sfmodel_exp or create_sfmodel_hn and adds the draws to it.

add_posterior_coefficients(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel_exp'
add_posterior_coefficients(
  object,
  posterior_function = NULL,
  keep_u = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel_hn'
add_posterior_coefficients(
  object,
  posterior_function = NULL,
  keep_u = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

an object of class "sfmodel_exp" or "sfmodel_hn", usually the result of a call to create_sfmodel_exp in combination with add_priors and add_initial_values.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

posterior_function

the function to be applied to the model in argument object. If NULL, the package's own sampler is used. It is called as posterior_function(object) and must return the object with its posterior element added.

keep_u

whether to store the inefficiency draws. Required by efficiency, but note that the stored object grows with the number of units times the number of retained draws.

verbose

either FALSE, TRUE for progress at every ten per cent of iterations, or an integer reporting interval.

Value

The object in object with the element posterior added. Each of its elements is a list whose element coeffs holds the draws after burn-in as an mcmc object with one row per draw and one column per parameter:

beta

the frontier coefficients, one column per regressor.

sigma_v

the standard deviation of the symmetric error.

lambda or sigma_u

the parameter of the inefficiency distribution, named for the model: the rate for the exponential specification and the scale for the half-normal one.

u

the inefficiency terms, one column per unit, if keep_u is TRUE.

Details

Each sweep draws the inefficiency terms from their truncated normal full conditionals, the frontier coefficients from a normal conditioning on \(y + u\) rather than \(y\), and the variance parameters from gamma distributions. This is the data augmentation scheme of van den Broeck, Koop, Osiewalski and Steel (1994).

Treating \(u\) as a latent variable rather than integrating it out means the efficiency scores come out of the sampler as draws, so efficiency reports genuine posterior distributions. Maximum likelihood has to fall back on the Jondrow et al. (1982) conditional mean, a point predictor of an unobserved quantity with no comparable measure of uncertainty.

The sampler draws with the seed in object$model$seed, which add_initial_values sets and add_seed replaces. R's random number generator is set to that seed for the simulation and put back as it was afterwards, so a call of set.seed() between add_initial_values() and this function does not change the draws. A model without a seed draws from R's generator as it stands.

Priors must have been added. Initial values are added with the default method if they are missing, since least squares starting values are a safe choice where no prior is.

References

Jondrow, J., Lovell, C. A. K., Materov, I. S., & Schmidt, P. (1982). On the estimation of technical inefficiency in the stochastic frontier production function model. Journal of Econometrics, 19(2–3), 233–238.

van den Broeck, J., Koop, G., Osiewalski, J., & Steel, M. F. J. (1994). Stochastic frontier models: A Bayesian perspective. Journal of Econometrics, 61(2), 273–303.

See also

add_posterior_loglik, efficiency, summary.sfmodel

Other posterior simulation: add_posterior_coefficients.sfmodel4_exp(), add_posterior_loglik.sfmodel4()

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf(n = 200, beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3), sigma_v = 0.2, par_u = 4)

model <- create_sfmodel_exp(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d,
                            iterations = 500, burnin = 200)
model <- add_priors(model)
model <- add_initial_values(model)
model <- add_posterior_coefficients(model)

summary(model)
#> Bayesian stochastic frontier model
#> 
#> Call:
#> create_sfmodel_exp(formula = y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, iterations = 500, 
#>     burnin = 200)
#> 
#> Frontier:           production
#> Inefficiency:       exponential
#> Observations:       200
#> Units:              200
#> Draws:              500 after 200 burn-in, thinning 1
#> 
#> Posterior summary, 95% credible bands:
#>               mean     sd   2.5% median  97.5%
#> (Intercept) 0.9820 0.0329 0.9185 0.9835 1.0460
#> x1          0.5048 0.0190 0.4688 0.5045 0.5431
#> x2          0.3045 0.0182 0.2666 0.3059 0.3361
#> sigma_v     0.1852 0.0243 0.1458 0.1830 0.2369
#> lambda      3.9853 0.5711 3.0847 3.9219 5.2840
#> 
#> Posterior mean efficiency, per observation:
#>   mean    min median    max 
#> 0.7969 0.2370 0.8400 0.9422
